title: Application for Child Abroad
subtitle: Petition for Alien Relative (Child)
description: sponsoring your child who is currently abroad to come to the United States

sections.title: Petitioner (U.S. Citizen or Green Card Holder) Documents

documents.name: Proof of U.S. citizenship OR green card (front and back)
documents.hint: U.S. citizens: upload your U.S. passport bio page, birth certificate, or Certificate of Naturalization. Green card holders: upload both the front and back of your Permanent Resident Card (I-551 / green card).

documents.name: Government-issued photo ID
documents.hint: Upload a valid state driver's license, state ID card, or U.S. passport showing your full legal name, date of birth, and photo.

documents.name: Child's birth certificate showing sponsoring parent's name
documents.hint: Upload the child's official birth certificate that lists your name as a parent. If the certificate is not in English, include a certified English translation.

documents.name: If adopted: final adoption decree + proof of legal custody and residency before age 16
documents.hint: For adopted children, upload the final court adoption decree plus documentation proving the child resided with you before their 16th birthday (e.g., school records, medical records at the same address).

documents.name: If stepchild: marriage certificate between parent and stepparent + proof of prior marriage terminations
documents.hint: Upload the marriage certificate between the stepparent and the child's biological parent, plus divorce decrees or death certificates for any prior marriages of either party.

documents.name: Paternal or maternal DNA test result from a USCIS-approved lab
documents.hint: If the parent-child relationship cannot be proven through standard documents, a DNA test from an AABB-accredited laboratory may be used. Contact us before arranging a DNA test to ensure it meets USCIS requirements.

sections.title: At Least Five (5) of the Following — Required

documents.name: Medical/health records showing parent and child's names
documents.hint: Examples: hospital birth records, vaccination records, or health insurance cards listing both parent and child's names.

documents.name: Church or religious records listing parent and child's name
documents.hint: Examples: baptism certificate, church membership or Sunday school enrollment records listing the parent and child.

documents.name: Insurance records naming both petitioner and beneficiary
documents.hint: Upload insurance policies (health, life, or auto) that list both the petitioner and the child, demonstrating a family relationship.

documents.name: Employment records showing parent and child's names
documents.hint: Examples: employer benefit enrollment forms listing children as dependents, or HR emergency contact forms listing the child.

documents.name: Financial records (tax returns) listing parent and child's name
documents.hint: Upload relevant pages from IRS tax returns (Form 1040) that list the child as a dependent.

documents.name: Census or tribal records in both names
documents.hint: Upload census household records or tribal enrollment documents listing both parent and child.

documents.name: Government records or ID documents showing names of both
documents.hint: Examples: school enrollment records listing the parent, military records, or any government document that ties the parent and child together.

documents.name: Proof of ongoing parent-child relationship (money transfers/remittance)
documents.hint: Upload receipts of money transfers or remittances sent to the child or their caretaker, demonstrating ongoing financial support across borders.

documents.name: Passport biographic page
documents.hint: Upload a scan of the child's passport page showing their full name, date of birth, nationality, and passport number. The passport should be valid.

documents.name: Marriage certificate, divorce decree, adoption decree, or court order for name changes (if applicable)
documents.hint: Upload any documents that explain name discrepancies or changes in family circumstances relevant to the child's petition.
